Tests.Name: One song from each tempo group
Tests.Subsystem: The 100 and 120 bpm switch containers and their meter overrides
Tests.Purpose: Three tempo groups were recovered from the banks. If the meter override is misread, the tempos will not differ audibly.
Tests.ExpectedTelemetry: the behaviour runs to completion and the song is cut by its Stop event
Tests.ExpectedPhysical: Bingo is cut at about 9.8 s by its Stop event, and the tempo audibly differs from A.
Tests.BlockedReason: A (Cozmo sings) was inconclusive, and A2 depends on it

Tests.Name: Sustained singing and a parameter posted mid-note
Tests.Subsystem: The streaming render: how far ahead it runs, what the scheduler sends, and what the robot plays
Tests.Purpose: The core review changed who waits for whom in the audio path twice: the scheduler now refuses to send samples that have not been rendered, and the render follows consumption rather than the wall clock. The failure modes that leaves are audible and only audible - chopping, a hanging note, an underrun - and they need a song long enough to expose them under the robot's real back-pressure. The vibrato parameter is posted while a note is already sounding, which is the whole reason the song is rendered as it plays.
Tests.ExpectedTelemetry: frames rendered, ready, sent and robot-reported played all advance together, with no underruns
Tests.ExpectedPhysical: Continuous sound with no alternating silence, no note that hangs or repeats, no reverb-like smear, and an audible change when the vibrato is posted.
Tests.BlockedReason: A (Cozmo sings) was inconclusive, and A3 depends on it

Tests.Name: Head, lift and a short drive
Tests.Subsystem: SetHeadAngle, SetLiftHeight, DriveWheels and the robot's own action acknowledgements
Tests.Purpose: The first check where he moves under his own power, and the floor under every movement test after it. It is deliberately small: if the head and lift do not go where they are told, nothing about docking or navigation can be interpreted.
Tests.ExpectedTelemetry: a MotorActionAck for each commanded move and a checked stop at the end
Tests.ExpectedPhysical: The head tilts down and back, the lift rises and lowers, then he drives forward a few centimetres and back, and stops. Nothing keeps moving afterwards.
Prerequisites: a clear, flat surface with no drop at the edge
Tests.BlockedReason: D (Lift position readout) has not run yet, and MOV depends on it

Tests.Name: A live body shuffle stops at its duration
Tests.Subsystem: The animation scheduler's live keyframe path and the tick loop that serves its deadline
Tests.Purpose: Idle streams a body keyframe with a duration and nothing else drives the scheduler. Before the correction nothing called Advance in that state, so the stop never went out and the wheels ran until something else countermanded them. Offline the stop is asserted against the message log; on the robot the wheels either stop or they do not.
Tests.ExpectedTelemetry: the reported wheel speeds go non-zero and return to zero within a frame or two of the duration
Tests.ExpectedPhysical: He shuffles forward for about a second and stops by himself. He does not keep creeping.
Tests.BlockedReason: MOV (Head, lift and a short drive) is blocked, and CR1 depends on it

Tests.Name: Idle keeps him alive without wandering
Tests.Subsystem: The idle behaviour: keep-alive blinks, small body shuffles and head moves
Tests.Purpose: Idle is what runs whenever nothing else does, so a fault here shows up as the robot looking dead or as it drifting across the table over minutes. Neither is visible in one clip.
Tests.ExpectedTelemetry: idle decisions print and no behaviour is left running at the end
Tests.ExpectedPhysical: He blinks and makes small movements, and he is still roughly where he started after a minute. Nothing repeats mechanically and nothing runs on.
Tests.BlockedReason: CR1 (A live body shuffle stops at its duration) is blocked, and IDL depends on it

Tests.Name: A cancelled animation stops sending
Tests.Subsystem: The scheduler's emission gate: a command of a cancelled playback must not get out
Tests.Purpose: The generation check was made under the lock and the command sent after it was released. A cancel landing in that window let one animation's motion go out in the middle of another. On the robot that is exactly what it looks like: a twitch after everything should have stopped.
Tests.ExpectedTelemetry: after the stop settles, wheel speed stays at zero and head and lift stop changing
Tests.ExpectedPhysical: He stops when the animation is cut and stays stopped. No late twitch of the head, the lift or the wheels.
Tests.BlockedReason: MOV (Head, lift and a short drive) is blocked, and CR3 depends on it

Tests.Name: A dropped link ends the animation, not the process
Tests.Subsystem: The animation tick loop's failure boundary when the robot goes away mid-clip
Tests.Purpose: The tick loop runs on a background thread and every frame reaches the transport. Once the link is gone the send throws, and before the correction that exception escaped a background thread and took the process with it. This is the one check where the disconnect is the subject, so the runner does not treat it as an interruption.
Tests.ExpectedTelemetry: the animation task completes, the ticker stops, and the failure is reported through Faulted
Tests.ExpectedPhysical: He stops where he is when the link goes, and the runner carries on to the next check rather than dying.

Tests.Name: Mount the charger
Tests.Subsystem: The charger object, the align dock with the real 20 x 27 mm marker, and the backwards mount
Tests.Purpose: The core review found the docking solve was building its object points from the marker's width in both directions, so the charger's 20 x 27 marker was solved as a square and came out 220 mm away when it was 286. It runs early, before the long manipulation sequence, so a failure is found in the first half hour.
Tests.ExpectedTelemetry: the charger is located with a pose, the align dock runs, docking error signals are sent, and the contacts report on charger
